description: First statutory reference load: the 1 March 2026 wage floors, the SARS 2027 tax year tables, the contribution parameters, and public holidays for 2026 and 2027. Researched from primary sources on 13 September 2026. NOT verified - every figure must be checked against the source document before this version can come into force.

sector_area.name: Area A - listed Metropolitan and Local Councils
sector_area.description: Metropolitan Councils: City of Cape Town, Greater East Rand Metro, City of Johannesburg, Tshwane and Nelson Mandela. Local Council: Emfuleni, Merafong, Mogale City, Metsimaholo, Randfontein, Stellenbosch, Westonaria. The gazette prints the metros and the local councils in ONE column, not two - see municipality_area_map for the list as loaded.

sector_area.name: Area B - KwaZulu-Natal
sector_area.description: All Areas in KwaZulu-Natal. The gazette states no figure: conditions of employment and minimum wage rates for KwaZulu-Natal areas are subject to the collective agreement concluded in the Bargaining Council for the Contract Cleaning Service Industry (BCCCI).

sector_area.name: Area C - the rest of the RSA
sector_area.description: In the rest of the RSA. This is a RESIDUAL, not a list: anywhere that is neither one of the Area A councils nor in KwaZulu-Natal. It is therefore the area most contract cleaning workplaces fall into, and it has no municipality_area_map rows by design.

minimum_wage_rate.source_reference: GN R.7083, GG 54075, 3 February 2026 (National Minimum Wage Act 9 of 2018)
minimum_wage_rate.notes: The general National Minimum Wage, and the floor beneath every sector. The gazette states an hourly figure only.

minimum_wage_rate.source_reference: GN R.7083, GG 54075, 3 February 2026 (National Minimum Wage Act 9 of 2018)
minimum_wage_rate.notes: Domestic workers are at the general National Minimum Wage, not below it. Stored as its own row rather than resolved through the NMW fallback so that the sector's figure is explicit and a future divergence is a data load.

minimum_wage_rate.source_reference: GN R.7083, GG 54075, 3 February 2026 (National Minimum Wage Act 9 of 2018)
minimum_wage_rate.notes: Weekly and monthly figures stored as gazetted, not recomputed. Weekly is on a 45-hour week and monthly on 4.333 weeks, per the gazette's own footnotes. Applies to the listed metros AND the listed local councils - both sit in this one column.

minimum_wage_rate.source_reference: GN R.7083, GG 54075, 3 February 2026 (National Minimum Wage Act 9 of 2018)
minimum_wage_rate.notes: Weekly and monthly figures stored as gazetted, not recomputed. THIS IS THE RESIDUAL RATE - the rest of the RSA, which is most of the country. Area B (KwaZulu-Natal) deliberately has no row: the gazette gives it no figure and points at the BCCCI agreement.

SARS Rates of Tax for Individuals, 2027 tax year (1 March 2026 - 28 February 2027)
paye_tax_bracket.notes: SARS prints this band's lower bound one rand higher. It is stored as the 'taxable income above R' figure the calculation actually uses, so no rand falls between two bands. The two readings agree at the boundary by construction: the previous band's tax at its ceiling equals this band's base.

medical_tax_credit_rate.source_reference: SARS Medical Tax Credit Rates, 2027 tax year (1 March 2026 - 28 February 2027)
medical_tax_credit_rate.notes: SARS publishes R376 for the taxpayer and R752 for the taxpayer and one dependant. Stored per tier: R376 main member, R376 first dependant, R254 each additional.

statutory_parameter.source_reference: Unemployment Insurance Contributions Act 4 of 2002, s6(1)(a)
Unemployment Insurance Contributions Act 4 of 2002, s6(1)(a)(ii)
Determination under s6(2) of the Unemployment Insurance Contributions Act 4 of 2002, Government Gazette 44641 of 28 May 2021, effective 1 June 2021
statutory_parameter.notes: VERIFY THE GAZETTE NUMBER - not confirmed from a primary source. Unchanged since 1 June 2021, which is the point: this ceiling moves on ministerial notice with no fixed calendar and is the parameter most often missed.

statutory_parameter.source_reference: Skills Development Levies Act 9 of 1999, s3(1)
statutory_parameter.notes: effective_from is the start of this reference data rather than the levy's commencement, which was not confirmed from a primary source.

statutory_parameter.source_reference: Skills Development Levies Act 9 of 1999, s4(b)
statutory_parameter.notes: FORWARD-LOOKING. The test is whether the employer reasonably believes leviable amounts over the NEXT twelve months will exceed this figure. It cannot be computed from payroll history, and any attempt to derive it from last year's payroll is wrong. effective_from is the start of this reference data, not the provision's commencement.

statutory_parameter.source_reference: Compensation Fund maximum amount of earnings, 2026/2027 assessment year (1 March 2026 - 28 February 2027)
statutory_parameter.notes: VERIFY AGAINST THE GAZETTE - this figure comes from a payroll vendor's published table, not from the notice itself. It is the least well sourced number in this load.

statutory_parameter.source_reference: GN 5970, GG 52232, March 2025 (Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997, s6(3))
statutory_parameter.notes: In force for the first two months of this reference version. A high earner loses only s18(3) - they keep the public holiday pay entitlement.

statutory_parameter.source_reference: GN 7384, GG 54544, 17 April 2026 (Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997, s6(3))

statutory_parameter.notes: Still 15 percent. The increases announced in the 2025 Budget were withdrawn and the 2026 Budget did not reinstate them. effective_from is the start of this reference data.

public_holiday.name: National Women's Day
public_holiday.notes: National Women's Day fell on Sunday 09 August 2026; the Act makes the following Monday the public holiday.

public_holiday.name: Human Rights Day
public_holiday.notes: Human Rights Day fell on Sunday 21 March 2027; the Act makes the following Monday the public holiday.

public_holiday.name: Day of Goodwill
public_holiday.notes: Day of Goodwill fell on Sunday 26 December 2027; the Act makes the following Monday the public holiday.

statutory_watch_item.name: National Minimum Wage and sectoral schedules
statutory_watch_item.description: The NMW Commission's recommendation is gazetted for comment and then finally, effective 1 March. Check the general rate, the EPWP rate and the contract cleaning schedule, which moves with it.
statutory_watch_item.source_name: Department of Employment and Labour gazette

statutory_watch_item.name: PAYE brackets, rebates, thresholds and medical credits
statutory_watch_item.description: Announced in the Budget and effective 1 March. All four move together; a year where the brackets are unchanged still needs the medical credits checked.
statutory_watch_item.source_name: SARS rates of tax for individuals

statutory_watch_item.name: BCEA earnings threshold
statutory_watch_item.description: Determined under s6(3) and usually effective 1 April or 1 May, on its own calendar rather than the tax year's.
statutory_watch_item.source_name: Department of Employment and Labour gazette

statutory_watch_item.name: UIF contribution ceiling
statutory_watch_item.description: Moves on ministerial notice with NO fixed calendar - it sat unchanged from October 2012 to June 2021 and has not moved since. The parameter most often missed in South African payroll, precisely because there is no date to watch.
statutory_watch_item.source_name: Department of Employment and Labour gazette

statutory_watch_item.name: COIDA maximum amount of earnings
statutory_watch_item.description: Increased by the Minister for each assessment year, usually announced shortly before the Return of Earnings season opens.

statutory_watch_item.name: Public holidays, including proclaimed once-off days
statutory_watch_item.description: The twelve statutory days are computable, but election days and days of mourning are proclaimed with little notice and follow no rule. Load the next calendar year each December.
statutory_watch_item.source_name: Public Holidays Act and Presidential proclamations

statutory_watch_item.name: Contract cleaning KwaZulu-Natal collective agreement
statutory_watch_item.description: Area B (KwaZulu-Natal) has no gazetted figure. Its wages come from the BCCCI collective agreement, which is extended by the Minister and runs on its own cycle. NOT YET LOADED - the agreement is needed before any KwaZulu-Natal contract cleaning employer can be onboarded.
statutory_watch_item.source_name: Bargaining Council for the Contract Cleaning Service Industry
